brief.title: The Lighthouse (child nodes)
brief.subject: A sample story for the horizontal timeline

nodes.title: Ada arrives in the harbour town
nodes.desc: She takes a room above the chandler's.

nodes.title: Ben writes from the city
nodes.desc: He has not yet decided to come.

nodes.title: The keeper's warning
nodes.desc: Stay off the point after dark.

nodes.title: The great storm
nodes.desc: The night the harbour wall broke.

nodes.title: The lamp goes dark
nodes.desc: The keeper's lamp fails at the worst hour.

nodes.title: Ada meets Ben at the quay
Ada reads the old logbooks
nodes.desc: She finds the night of the storm.

nodes.title: The town council meets
nodes.desc: The lighthouse is to be repaired.

nodes.title: The lamp is lit again
nodes.desc: The point is bright for the first time in twenty years.

nodes.title: Ben goes back to the city
nodes.desc: The repairs are done; his work is elsewhere.

nodes.title: The keeper's two conditions
nodes.desc: He names two conditions for staying on the point at night: the lamp must be lit, and nobody goes past the second rock.

nodes.title: The lamp stays lit
nodes.desc: The first condition: whoever stays keeps the lamp burning until dawn.

nodes.title: Past the second rock
nodes.desc: The second condition: the tide covers the path beyond the second rock within the hour.

nodes.title: The vote
nodes.desc: Seven to two to relight the lamp at the town's expense.

nodes.title: Ada's statement
nodes.desc: Ada reads from the logbooks and names the nights the lamp was dark.

nodes.title: The 1870 entry
nodes.desc: The storm night, written in the keeper's own hand: lamp out at midnight.
